content.value_statement: pnpm projects often need precise commands, workspace settings, and migration rules. This skill gives current guidance for installs, CI, catalogs, patches, and secure configuration.
actual_capabilities: Explains pnpm install, add, update, remove, run, dlx, publish, and audit workflows.
Guides workspace setup with pnpm-workspace.yaml, filters, shared lockfiles, catalogs, and packageConfigs.
Helps migrate npm or Yarn projects to pnpm and update configuration for recent versions.
Describes CI caching, frozen lockfiles, Docker use, and store path handling.
Covers security controls such as allowBuilds, minimumReleaseAge, trust policy, and lockfile integrity.
Explains patches, overrides, aliases, hooks, config dependencies, and the global virtual store.
limitations: It provides guidance only; it does not install packages or edit files unless the host agent chooses to act.
It does not replace testing after dependency changes or migrations.
It cannot verify unpublished package behavior or private registry policies without project access.
It is based on documented pnpm behavior and may need updates when pnpm changes.

use_cases.title: Set up a workspace
use_cases.description: Create or review pnpm-workspace.yaml, filters, catalogs, and lockfile strategy for a monorepo.

use_cases.title: Harden CI installs
use_cases.description: Choose frozen installs, safe caching, Corepack setup, and package build approval for pipelines.

use_cases.title: Migrate package managers
use_cases.description: Plan a move from npm or Yarn to pnpm while preserving auth, scripts, and dependency behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Install dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pnpm skill to explain the safest install command for this project and which files I should check first.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my pnpm workspace plan and suggest settings for packages, catalogs, peer dependencies, and shared scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration checklist for moving this npm or Yarn project to pnpm, including config, lockfiles, and CI changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit dependency policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this pnpm dependency policy for build approvals, release age controls, overrides, patches, and private registry handling.

output_examples.input: I need reliable CI installs for a pnpm monorepo.
output: Recommends Corepack, a frozen lockfile, and workspace-aware install steps.
Explains why the pnpm store is cached instead of node_modules.
Suggests filters for changed-package test jobs.

output_examples.input: We want to migrate a Yarn workspace to pnpm.
output: Lists files to remove or convert during migration.
Moves settings into pnpm-workspace.yaml and keeps auth in ignored npm config files.
Adds checks for phantom dependencies and peer dependency behavior.

output_examples.input: Our team needs one dependency version across packages.
output: Compares catalogs, overrides, and package extensions.
Recommends a central version policy that matches the requested workflow.

best_practices: Keep install settings in pnpm-workspace.yaml and keep auth tokens in ignored npm config files.
Use frozen lockfiles in CI and review lockfile changes during dependency updates.
Prefer catalogs, overrides, and packageExtensions before writing custom hooks.
anti_patterns: Do not commit registry tokens or private auth files.
Do not cache node_modules across CI jobs when the pnpm store cache is enough.
Do not enable broad build-script execution without reviewing the package list.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with pnpm commands, workspaces, CI setup, migrations, dependency policy, and current configuration files.

faq.question: Can it edit my project automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance. File edits depend on the agent, permissions, and your request.

faq.question: Does it cover pnpm workspaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers workspace packages, filters, shared lockfiles, catalogs, packageConfigs, and common monorepo workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace pnpm documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes relevant behavior for agent workflows and should be checked against current pnpm releases when needed.

faq.question: How should private registry tokens be handled?
faq.answer: Keep tokens in ignored auth files or environment-backed user config, and avoid printing token values in agent output.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
